entries.summary: Grand two-cover proof program: minimum-counterexample reductions, quadratic-minimum regimes, deletion-state and defect-span interfaces, support-reconfiguration and pairwise-repartition routes, and bounded transport or obstruction mechanisms aimed at reducing spanning covers to two paths.
entries.title: Grand two-cover conjecture

entries.summary: No-trapping reduction through deletion-generated three-side states: singleton lifts descend to canonical three-side states, and the descendants develop transport, reversal, and bounded escape mechanisms intended to rule out trapped repartition components.
entries.title: The grand theorem reduces to no trapping of deletion-generated three-side states

entries.summary: Current finite-kernel defect-compression composition connecting deletion states, bounded obstruction taxonomies, endpoint transport, and the remaining global closure gap.
entries.title: Current proof composition: bounded obstruction to defect compression

entries.summary: Global quadratic-minimum proof-rehearsal frontier: reduce a minimum counterexample to a small set of component-size regimes, convert staircase profiles into small Hamiltonian supports, reversals, or transport disturbance, and route the remaining near-balanced regimes into standard closure interfaces.
entries.title: Proof-rehearsal frontier: five surviving global quadratic-minimum regimes

entries.summary: Dense five-window gluing over a fixed tight core: repeated Hamiltonian five-set stars are synchronized into endpoint extenders, alternating fans, four-grids, or a second large path, with the central issue being compatibility of Hamilton orders rather than support counts alone.
entries.title: Dense five-window gluing over a fixed core

entries.summary: Maximin and deletion-side structure, including dense central-deletion disturbance, minimum-side/maximin coupling, sharp exchange blockade, and barrier normalization.
entries.title: Maximin and balanced-cover compression

entries.summary: Sparse clean-deletion augmentation branch: clean augmentations cannot persist densely; recurrent central-path destruction, short block-faithful runs, and forced multi-crossing among deep-central deletions provide the obstruction needed for maximin compression.
entries.title: Clean deletion augmentations are sparse, forcing recurrent central path destruction

entries.summary: Terminal quadratic-minimum frontier: canonical closure witnesses eliminate structureless neutral transport; the remaining unique-large and unique-small residues localize to donor insertion gaps or short aligned transfer cycles and then force standard transport disturbance, order disagreement, reverse crossing, or a bounded Hamiltonian window.
entries.title: Terminal quadratic minima reduce to canonical closure witnesses or an aligned same-end neutral transfer

entries.summary: Aligned neutral-transfer cycle branch: repeated vertices in nonbacktracking aligned transfer walks arise quickly; the unique-small residue then forces cross-core triples, core crossings, four-windows, or a standard transport disturbance.
entries.title: Aligned neutral-transfer cycles force a repeated vertex or order disagreement

entries.summary: Unconditional route around the canonical defect-span-three interface. Minimum counterexamples have defect span exactly three; opposite longest-path endpoint deletion covers always expose support/order disagreement. With positive deletion slack, every central deletion reduces to crossing, order disagreement, or same-slot replacement; comparing the two endpoint anchors shows that at most two central labels can remain same-slot from both ends. The general pair-deletion reconstruction lemma isolates the underlying reason: two distinct ordered block structures can be equalized by deleting at most two labels. Thus repeated clean replacement is no longer the main bulk obstruction. The current closure gap is to consume the resulting support crossings and order reversals into endpoint absorption or defect span at most two.
entries.title: Defect-span three and deletion-cover compatibility give the canonical global obstruction interface

entries.summary: Anchored four-window transport route: every deletion state is driven to a Hamiltonian four-window or bounded barrier, then repeated endpoint exchanges, five- and six-window amplification, and short label migration reduce nonescaping states to order disagreement, strict descent, or a coherent endpoint-square obstruction.
entries.title: Every deletion state reduces to a Hamiltonian four-window, the universal cyclic four-kernel, or a doubled cross barrier

entries.summary: Anchored Hamiltonian four-window route: every vertex lies in a Hamiltonian four-set inside every containing five-set, and in a minimum counterexample each such four-set has a non-Hamiltonian path-cover-two complement; descendants exploit overlapping windows, endpoint exchanges, and bounded support migration.
entries.title: Every vertex has a Hamiltonian four-window inside every containing five-set

entries.summary: Large four-side escape package: above order fourteen a Hamiltonian four-side must descend, enlarge to a six-window, or create order disagreement; descendants turn six-windows and shared-endpoint exchanges into bounded migration and further escape.
entries.title: Above order fourteen every Hamiltonian four-side escapes by descent, a Hamiltonian six-window, or order disagreement

entries.summary: Nonescaping anchored four-window amplification: above order fourteen a four-window must descend, disagree, or migrate only a few labels; failure to escape amplifies through an adjacent five-union and two-label endpoint-square structure until the residual coherent square is exposed.
entries.title: Above order fourteen every anchored four-window descends, disagrees, or migrates by at most two labels

entries.summary: Deletion-cover incompatibility forcing: turn sparse or structured compatibility neighborhoods into uniform incompatibility families, endpoint transport constraints, and bounded obstruction patterns that feed the global deletion-state closure route.
entries.title: Deletion-cover incompatibility forcing

entries.summary: Local geometry of compatibility neighborhoods: each neighborhood is a path/cycle system in which incompatible pairs localize at the anchor, high degree forces synchronized incompatibility bursts, and separated neighbors create long intervals of order reversal.
entries.title: Compatibility neighborhoods are unions of paths and cycles

entries.summary: Defect-span local-search route: lexicographically minimal spanning orders and quadratic-minimal three-covers are pushed through local swaps, endpoint complements, canonical central 3/5 states, and size-gap descent toward defect span at most two.
entries.title: Defect-span local-search theorem

entries.summary: Global four-side quadratic-minimum program: a minimum four-side locks both endpoints against both long paths, creating rigid cross-endpoint six-sets, endpoint five-set grids, reversal families, transport packages, and the remaining 4|4|a / 4|5|a profile analysis.
entries.title: Global quadratic minima have minimum side four, and a four-side locks both endpoints against both long paths

entries.summary: Rigid six-set and endpoint-grid branch at a global four-side minimum: cross-endpoint pairs form non-Hamiltonian six-sets, four-side labels stay noninsertable into both long paths, and endpoint-pair grids, doubled barriers, and imbalance gains drive the four-side/five-side continuation toward Hamiltonian kernels or order disagreement.
entries.title: Every cross-endpoint pair around a global quadratic minimum with a four-vertex component forms a rigid non-Hamiltonian six-set

entries.summary: Endpoint-pair grid imbalance route for global four-side minima: every grid cell has a more imbalanced complementary two-cover, yielding sharp-half-order profile restrictions and, after secondary balancing, elimination of persistent four-sides and transition to the five-side continuation.
entries.title: Every endpoint-pair grid cell has a strictly more imbalanced two-cover complement

entries.summary: Five-side continuation of the quadratic-minimum program: after excluding persistent four-sides, endpoint-pair replacement grids on a five-side are used to force descent, order disagreement, or a larger Hamiltonian support in the remaining global minima.
entries.title: Five-side quadratic-minimum continuation

entries.summary: Four-four quadratic-profile continuation: the 4|4|a and neighboring 4|5|a profiles are analyzed through synchronized endpoint extensions, neutral cyclic exchanges, and locked-label geometries, eliminating large 4|4 profiles and reducing the 4|5 plateau to finite structured residues.
entries.title: Four-four quadratic profile continuation

entries.summary: Deletion-family crossing producers: support-compatible deletion families force synchronized endpoint crossing multiplicity or order disagreement.
entries.title: Support-compatible deletion families force synchronized endpoint crossing multiplicity or order disagreement

entries.summary: Canonical central-bridge no-trapping route: deletion states reach bounded central bridges, where strict descent and bridge-controlled geometry must prevent trapping.
entries.title: Every deletion state has a canonical bounded central-bridge three-cover

entries.summary: Supported endpoint-transport and barrier inputs: deletion-cover dynamics, endpoint hooks, codimension packages, compatible-triangle residues, and fixed-label transport.
entries.title: Deletion-cover dynamics

entries.summary: End-adjacent replacement obstruction: clean replacement at an end is impossible, and the equality-two-crossing residue collapses to a few order-neutral block forms whose descendants expose the remaining crossing and order constraints.
entries.title: End-adjacent clean replacement is impossible

entries.summary: Endpoint transport and local obstruction geometry: endpoint hooks, replacement and pivot structure, bounded reverse windows, mixed Hamiltonian windows, cross barriers, local connectors, and truncation-or-lock alternatives.
entries.title: Endpoint transport and local obstruction geometry

entries.summary: Codimension-five structural package for endpoint normalization and bounded obstruction localization.
entries.title: Codimension-five endpoint normalization

entries.summary: Endpoint-hook forcing package: deletion covers impose canonical hooks at both ends of the complementary path, and the descendants combine these hooks into local connector, barrier, and transport configurations.
entries.title: Endpoint hook forcing

entries.summary: Endpoint transport and defect compression: ordered endpoint covers, support/order disagreement, short transport, compatible-triangle and rooted-graph structure, codimension shells, and bounded obstruction routes toward compressing the defect span.
entries.title: Endpoint-transport / defect-compression bridge

entries.summary: Well-founded defect-window transport: local obstruction windows are organized into a descending transport process whose branches expose support migration, endpoint reversals, bounded locks, or a strict reduction of the relevant defect measure.
entries.title: Well-founded defect-window transport

entries.summary: Deficit-one corridor route: order-preserving comparisons either descend or reverse immediately, or localize to one gap where a chain of parallel tight corridors is reduced to bounded disturbance, paired noninsertion, or a balanced longest-path exchange.
entries.title: Deficit-one order-preserving comparisons either descend, reverse, or localize to one corridor gap

entries.summary: Compatibility-window transport inside the well-founded defect process: compatible anchor neighbors occupy a short interval, after which degree, isolation, incompatibility, and four-kernel alternatives drive the transport toward bounded disturbance.
entries.title: Pairwise-compatible anchor neighbors occupy at most four consecutive positions

entries.summary: Anchor-neighborhood compatibility geometry: compatible deletion states form consecutive runs along one anchor path; endpoint-labeled edges then have tightly bounded common neighbors, leading to sparse compatibility, forced incompatibility, or the four-kernel frontier.
entries.title: Each anchor-neighborhood compatibility component is a consecutive run on one anchor path

entries.summary: Positional-lag branch for order-preserving longest-path intersections: encode omission and insertion displacement by bounded prefix balance, constrain how lag evolves along surviving runs, and use those constraints to expose crossing or transport when near-longest orders remain aligned.
entries.title: Order-preserving intersections with a longest path have bounded positional lag

entries.summary: Codimension-four structural package for Hamiltonian-side endpoint geometry and bounded obstruction localization.
entries.title: Codimension-four Hamiltonian-side structure

entries.summary: Endpoint-reversal obstruction branch: reduce endpoint reversals to a bounded four-vertex frontier or a universal two-end obstruction family, then use the resulting local reverse data to force transport, disagreement, or a bounded closure witness.
entries.title: Endpoint reversals reduce to a bounded four-vertex frontier or a universal two-end obstruction family

entries.summary: Hard endpoint-reversal grid: a universal reverse-cross family becomes a complete endpoint-pair extension grid, whose five- and six-support consequences force bounded Hamiltonian structure, order disagreement, or return to the classified four-vertex obstruction.
entries.title: The universal hard-reversal cross family is a complete endpoint pair grid with ubiquitous local order disagreement

entries.summary: Large-order trapped-minimum reduction to minimum side five: from order seventeen onward quadratic minima either exhibit order disagreement or enter the five-side regime, whose descendants develop common cores, endpoint grids, codimension shells, and bounded transport obstructions.
entries.title: From order seventeen onward trapped quadratic minima have minimum side five or order disagreement

entries.summary: Large-order minimum-side escalation: from order eighteen onward a trapped quadratic minimum either has side at least six or order disagreement; rooted six-side shells and successive order thresholds then raise the minimum side further or expose explicit local structure.
entries.title: From order eighteen onward trapped quadratic minima have minimum side six or order disagreement

entries.summary: Six-side bad-endpoint shell: shared four-cores from two failed endpoint extensions generate rooted six-support graphs whose adjacency, matching, and migration structure forces support motion, a neutral repartition, or order disagreement.
entries.title: Two bad endpoints over a six-side share three four-cores and force six-support migration or order disagreement

entries.summary: Minimum-side endpoint-deletion branch: classify each endpoint deletion as direct crossing, support-compatible restoration, or one rigid two-crossing block pattern, and propagate the rigid residue until it yields disagreement, reciprocal crossing, or bounded reverse structure.
entries.title: A minimum-side endpoint deletion has only direct crossing, support-compatible restoration, or one rigid two-crossing block configuration

entries.summary: Compatible-triangle and cyclic-four-kernel branch: endpoint-compatible triangles enter a radius-two stable cyclic-kernel residue, whose stable complements and comparison structure are used to force bounded disturbance or rule out neutral trapping.
entries.title: Endpoint compatible triangles enter the cyclic four-kernel frontier

entries.summary: Longest-path crossing producers: complementary endpoint covers force synchronized crossing, mixing, and rigid two-crossing geometry.
entries.title: Sharp half-order longest-support continuation

entries.summary: Equal-cover endpoint-probe analysis: probing opposite endpoints forces relative-order disagreement, reciprocal crossing, or a leave-and-return excursion; the hard all-equal residue localizes to wrap triples and bounded support configurations.
entries.title: Equal-cover endpoint probes force order disagreement, reciprocal crossing, or a leave-and-return excursion

entries.summary: Historical transport stress-test mathematics retained for comparison and possible reuse.
entries.title: Order-eleven stress test for transport

entries.summary: Defect-line dual-certificate program: fixed spanning orders reduce two-cover failure to size-two matchings in the defect line, while the descendants develop bounded cyclic defect certificates, run classifications, rotations, and deletion-state consequences aimed at making that obstruction global.
entries.title: The fixed-order dual certificate is a two-edge matching in the defect line

entries.summary: Cyclic defect-certificate classification at minimum defect span three: only five proper run geometries and one full-cycle case survive, and the descendant branches analyze isolated-defect cubes, all-equal support triangles, double-wrap rotations, deletion-state transport, and bounded obstruction shells.
entries.title: Minimum span three has a uniformly bounded cyclic defect certificate with only five run geometries

entries.summary: Three-isolated-defect cube interface: span-three defect orderings with three isolated cyclic defects form an exact singleton-transfer cube, whose interface slides, descent/transport trichotomy, and nested discrete-gradient geometry reduce the defect configuration to endpoint disturbance, neutral transport, or order disagreement.
entries.title: The three-isolated-defect case is an exact cube of singleton transfers

entries.summary: Three-isolated-defect cube program: use the discrete-gradient size parametrization of the eight cube states to classify neutral transfers and equality profiles, then force endpoint disturbance, support migration, or relative-order disagreement from the surviving cube geometry.
entries.title: The three-isolated-defect cube has an exact discrete-gradient size parametrization

entries.summary: All-equal matching-cube support-triangle program: antipodal equality produces three coupled Hamiltonian supports with blocked whole-path enlargement; reverse boundary triples, endpoint barriers, mixed supports, greedy transport, and coarse crossings then force a canonical disturbance or closure input.
entries.title: All-equal antipodal exchange yields the support triangle with blocked whole-path enlargements

entries.summary: All-equal support-triangle barrier branch: endpoint insertion or order disagreement closes immediately; otherwise synchronized endpoint barriers drive reverse hooks, mixed four- and five-path structure, support crossings, six-support families, and eventual relative-order disturbance.
entries.title: The all-equal support triangle yields endpoint insertion, order disagreement, or synchronized endpoint barriers

entries.summary: All-equal support-triangle disagreement branch: transferred-label insertion either fails with an explicit endpoint hook or succeeds along an antipodal singleton-transfer corridor; the surviving full-support alternatives force endpoint-edge reversals and hence relative-order disagreement.
entries.title: The all-equal support triangle always forces relative-order disagreement

entries.summary: Nonmatching cyclic-certificate double-wrap branch: proper nonmatching run types admit a rotation with two wrap defects, producing a four-vertex tight support with two-coverable complement and feeding deletion states into central/outer bridge, paired-obstruction, transport, and gap-network reductions.
entries.title: Every nonmatching proper cyclic defect certificate has a double-wrap rotation

entries.summary: Deletion-state paired-obstruction reduction: from order fifteen onward deletion states enter four-side descent or a finite paired-obstruction menu, which is refined into interval connectors, opposite crosses, fixed-endpoint matching fronts, mixed support, and complete gap networks.
entries.title: Every deletion state of order at least fifteen enters four-side descent or the finite paired-obstruction menu

entries.summary: Three-plus-two cyclic-defect branch: simultaneous central and wrap reversals give a small quadratic-potential landscape and direct access to four-side obstruction, repeated descent, persistent outer barriers, or a bounded transport kernel.
entries.title: The three-plus-two cyclic defect type has simultaneous central and wrap reversals

entries.summary: Deletion-cover cocycle route: compare singleton-swap states around compatibility cycles, separate support-level consistency from genuine order defects, and reduce nontrivial monodromy to omitted-label gap transport and the two-core transposition residue.
entries.title: Deletion-cover consistency cocycle

entries.summary: Support-level deletion-cover cocycle branch: singleton-swap cycles have trivial support monodromy while genuine order defects persist with controlled parity, forcing endpoint structure or a bounded order-transport normal form and showing that defects survive almost all further deletions.
entries.title: Support-level deletion-cover cocycles have trivial monodromy

entries.summary: Failed-splice clause-system route: exchange failures are encoded by bounded transition clauses whose overlaps force cross triples, pivot conflicts, or other rigid local structure, seeking closure by consistency or compressibility rather than by an ordinary support graph.
entries.title: Failed-splice exchange is naturally a bounded clause system, not a graph

entries.summary: One-defect support reconfiguration route, with frozen-support obstructions and deletion-level order disagreement retained above the more specialized reconfiguration subbranches.
entries.title: Alternative route: one-defect support reconfiguration

entries.summary: Ordered path arguments beyond support expansion: transfer invariants, support-only countermodels, and order-sensitive exchange structure.
entries.title: Astra guidance: ordered path arguments beyond support expansion

entries.summary: One-defect deletion-state reconfiguration: support expansion, alternating deletion moves, synchronized omission families, crossing producers, frozen-support obstructions, and the bridge from minimum deletion side to maximin compression.
entries.title: One-defect states are deletion covers with the omitted vertex restored

entries.summary: One-defect crossing-producer package: three-label producers collapse to a common four-core, while opposite endpoint exchanges produce a coupled square-triangle structure whose support triangle expands uniformly and whose commuting corner is isolated or forces a larger local clique.
entries.title: Three-label producers collapse to a four-core, while opposite endpoint exchanges force a longest-path and support-triangle package

entries.summary: Order-thirteen radius-three support-expansion program: capacity-six expansion, degree-two equality, isolated double-frozen odd edges, and coupled odd/Johnson graph inequalities are combined to rule out two-regular deficient-support behavior and force crossing or reconfiguration escape.
entries.title: Radius-three support expansion has capacity six, and degree-two equality is a sliding-triple system

entries.summary: Order-thirteen radius-three rigidity: odd-support degree, Hamiltonian-deletion multiplicity, and transfer cliques constrain equality cases in the deficient-support graph, with descendants forcing expansion, degree-three cyclic kernels, crossings, or escape from degree-two corridors.
entries.title: Odd-degree repulsion and transfer cliques rigidify radius-three equality

entries.summary: Alternating one-defect transfer dynamics: Hamiltonian deletions move the unique defect between the two supports, with minimum-support trapping characterized by frozen return moves; descendants develop large-side shell and rooted transport consequences of this transfer model.
entries.title: One-defect transfers are alternating Hamiltonian-deletion moves

entries.summary: Rooted-shell branch of supported transport: large minimum deletion sides produce rooted Hamiltonian shells and fixed-defect three-side transport.
entries.title: Rooted seven-set Hamiltonian shell graph

entries.summary: Small-deletion-side omission families: sides of order three through five yield at least four synchronized deletion labels, common endpoint hooks, Hamiltonian end fans, unavoidable order disagreement, and clean support exchanges, ruling out local frozen behavior in the small-side regime.
entries.title: Small deletion sides generate synchronized omission families

entries.summary: Weighted and fractional longest-path route: relate the weighted half-path principle to fractional path-cover threshold two, study laminar rounding and its obstructions, and use sharp-half-order deletion transversals, support incompatibility, and ordered disturbance to attack the equality shell.
entries.title: Weighted longest-path principle and fractional two-cover

entries.summary: Route-specific work on converting fractional path covers into two-covers by simplifying crossing positive-weight path supports. Laminar mass-at-most-two covers round immediately, and laminarization would exclude the sharp half-order shell; however union-Hamiltonian two-support replacement and generic radius-two replacement are unavailable, so any successful transformation must use sharper optimal-LP, ordered-path, or nonlocal structure.
entries.title: Uncross fractional path covers

entries.summary: Sharp-shell transversal and support-graph route: transversals of deletion covers reduce to forests or a single odd support cycle, and the descendants analyze degree, cycle, corridor, and repeated-label structure that forces disturbance or transport.
entries.title: Any transversal of sharp-shell deletion covers is a forest or one odd support cycle

entries.summary: A sustained route-specific line for the stronger equitable two-cover conjecture: minimum balanced failures force parity-specific noninsertability; odd-order compatible deletion states have one-gap geometry and sparse compatibility; density then forces a large uniform incompatibility family, with the order-compatible branch synchronizing to one fixed complementary Hamilton path.
entries.title: Balanced two-cover conjecture

entries.summary: Balanced-cover size and compatibility consequences inside the balanced-two-cover route, beginning with parity-specific noninsertability.
entries.title: Minimum balanced-cover failures force parity-specific noninsertability

entries.summary: Certified quadratic-potential and endpoint-transfer machinery for pairwise repartition, including order-independent descent, merge, transport, and reduction statements across arbitrary order.
entries.title: Pairwise repartition connects three-covers to two-covers

entries.summary: Quadratic-minimal endpoint-transfer blockade in the pairwise-repartition route: improving Hamiltonian endpoint transfers are forbidden, forcing size-gap obstructions, lower bounds on small sides, and a bounded menu of insertion or transport failures.
entries.title: Quadratic-minimal three-covers forbid Hamiltonian endpoint transfer

entries.summary: Size-gap obstruction program inside a quadratic-minimal three-cover: two bounded failed-insertion witnesses are amplified into small Hamiltonian kernels, cross triples, endpoint connectors, five-side common-core structure, or neutral-transfer cycles on a trapped plateau.
entries.title: Every quadratic-minimal size gap yields two bounded insertion obstructions

entries.summary: Five-side branch of the canonical central-bridge route, using a common four-vertex extension core and full-path insertion obstructions.
entries.title: A five-vertex side has a common four-vertex endpoint extension core

entries.summary: Five-side synchronization program: a five-vertex side synchronizes most surrounding endpoints; the descendants turn that synchronization into controlled swaps, insertion obstructions, far-end alignment, migration, and bounded disturbance sufficient to progress from a trapped five-side.
entries.title: A five-vertex side synchronizes at least three of four surrounding endpoints

entries.summary: Synchronized five-side replacement branch: equal-size swaps versus bounded insertion obstructions lead to canonical five-side/far-end synchronization, exact good-deletion patterns, migration bounds, and ultimately full-path obstruction or order disagreement.
entries.title: Synchronized five-side replacements give equal-size swaps or bounded insertion obstructions

entries.summary: Canonical five-side far-end synchronization branch: a central Hamiltonian five-side synchronizes the two outer endpoints; far-end exchanges, six-set residues, good-core deletion patterns, migration bounds, and rigid bridge obstructions are then used to force order disturbance, multiple crossing, a bounded common window, or entry to the four-side obstruction engine.
entries.title: Canonical five-vertex central components synchronize the two far endpoints

entries.summary: Synchronized far-end six-set branch: a successful far-end exchange creates a non-Hamiltonian six-set whose good deletion pattern has a fixed-pair structure; common four-cores, continuation labels, bounded common windows, and neutral 4-to-5 rotations then force order disturbance or controlled transport.
entries.title: A successful far-end exchange forces a non-Hamiltonian synchronized six-set

entries.summary: Quadratic size-gap barrier branch: a largest-second gap at a quadratic minimum yields a small Hamiltonian kernel, reversed-edge detour, or doubled cross barrier; the barrier alternative is propagated until a connector or further bounded obstruction appears.
entries.title: Every quadratic-minimal largest-second size gap forces a Hamiltonian kernel or doubled cross barrier

entries.summary: Astra pairwise-repartition singleton-transfer program: singleton residues generate a long reconfiguration line through plateau escape, quadratic minimality, endpoint transfer, balanced small-order shells, and eventual obstruction or connectivity results.
entries.title: Singleton-transfer endpoint residue is a two-step Astra repartition segment

entries.summary: Astra equality-plateau escape: reciprocal singleton transfers are converted into strict quadratic descent or a quadratic-minimal trapped state, after which pairwise balance extremality, 3|5 transport, and small-order omission-shell analysis drive the remaining branch.
entries.title: Reciprocal singleton-transfer states always escape the Astra equality plateau

entries.summary: Quadratic-potential reconfiguration inside the Astra pairwise-repartition route, where quadratic minimality converts trapping into pairwise balance extremality.
entries.title: Quadratic minimality reduces Astra trapping to pairwise balance extremality

entries.summary: Quadratic endpoint-transfer reduction to the 3|5 shell: transfer barriers force the canonical 3|5 regime, after which support expansion, balanced eight- and eleven-vertex shells, omission graphs, and endpoint obstructions are used to eliminate trapping.
entries.title: Quadratic endpoint-transfer barriers reduce a three-side to the 3|5 rotation shell

entries.summary: Edge-order and balanced-eight reduction inside the 3|5 route: trapped three-five configurations are pushed through eight-vertex balanced-cover structure and edge-order obstructions until only the universal order-eleven three-side barrier and its finite omission geometry remain.
entries.title: Edge-orderable eight-vertex unions cannot support a trapped 3|5 pair

entries.summary: Order-eleven 4|4|3 omission-surface program: complete pair reachability on the three-side generates a large family of singleton omission states, whose eight-, nine-, and ten-label shells are successively excluded or rigidified by common-core and fixed-side structure.
entries.title: The 4|4|3 plateau has complete pair reachability on its three-side

entries.summary: Order-eleven omission-surface continuation: large omission-label sets, targeted singleton attempts, and eight-label mutual bad-extension cores are used to connect equitable 5|5|1 states back to the 4|4|3 shell and rule out trapped omission geometry.
entries.title: Order-eleven omission-surface continuation

entries.summary: Order-eleven omission-label shell: many omission labels force strong five-side cohabitation and an eight-label omission graph; missing edges create reciprocal mobility and bad-swap saturation, while the complete-shell alternative is driven toward contradiction or restored mobility.
entries.title: The order-eleven Astra component has at least seven omission labels

entries.summary: Order-thirteen 3|5|5 mobility program: dense equal-size reachability forces many three-side supports, widespread vertex and pair participation, exchange rectangles, common-core stars, and quantitative support expansion that constrains any trapped plateau.
entries.title: Order-thirteen 3|5|5 plateaux have dense equal-size mobility and at least ninety-four three-side supports

entries.summary: Order-eleven balanced-state connectivity branch: all 5|5|1 and 4|4|3 states are driven into one Astra component, and the descendants analyze triple reachability and longest-path obstruction cases needed to rule out an order-eleven counterexample.
entries.title: All balanced order-eleven states lie in one Astra component

entries.summary: Longest-path complement route: analyze insertion-slot and positional-lag structure for near-longest paths, classify paired noninsertion outside a longest path, and seek either separated connector structure or concentrated bounded witnesses that force a Hamiltonian complement or compressible obstruction.
entries.title: A longest path can have a Hamiltonian complement

entries.summary: Prescribed-vertex separation route: study minimal failures to separate a specified pair by a two-cover, derive doubly blocked deletion states and cut barriers, and compress the obstruction to rigid two-crossing or small-support geometry.
entries.title: Two prescribed vertices can be separated by a two-cover

entries.summary: Edge-orderable-tournament route: normalize critical backward comparisons through comparison-flip structure, analyze the one-backward residue via endpoint-minimal mandatory-triple covers and their transfer barriers, and reduce the surviving equality cases to bounded mandatory-side and six-set obstructions.
entries.title: Edge-orderable tournaments suffice for extremal path-cover number

entries.summary: Comparison-arc criticality route: a minimal non-edge-orderable three-cover witness becomes critical under each backward comparison flip, leading to a one-backward residue, forced deletion-cover states, mandatory-triple structure, and precedence/order obstructions.
entries.title: A minimal non-edge-orderable three-cover witness is comparison-arc critical

entries.summary: Mandatory-triple cover calculus: normalization, Hamilton-order rigidity, endpoint-extension barriers, transfer obstructions, interval-complement obstructions, and re-extension localization.
entries.title: The one-backward Astra-010 residue produces an inseparable pair in an edge-orderable tournament

entries.summary: Mandatory-triple branch of the one-backward edge-orderable reduction: the corrected neighboring state has no singleton-side two-cover, so endpoint-minimal covers carrying the mandatory triple obey transfer blockades, Hall-type obstructions, lower bounds on the opposite side, and a rigid four/six-vertex kernel analysis.
entries.title: The corrected one-backward Astra-010 neighbor has no singleton-side two-cover

entries.summary: Locked mandatory-triple residue: the corrected one-backward neighbor has a two-sided locked triple component, forcing the opposite side to order at least four and reducing equality to a specific six-set residue around an endpoint-minimal mandatory triple.
entries.title: The corrected one-backward neighbor has a two-sided locked minimal triple component

entries.summary: Contiguous-block relocation route: analyze trapped three-path plateaux through quadratic extremality, endpoint transfers, neutral wraps, and size-gap restrictions, with the goal of forcing descent, a common-middle square, order disagreement, or another bounded obstruction.
entries.title: Contiguous block moves escape every three-path plateau

entries.summary: Core reusable toolkit: definitions, minimum-counterexample calculus, small-order structure, path restriction, cover surgery, insertion, local extension, edge-order methods, and related proof tools.
entries.title: Toolkit

entries.summary: Extremal Hamiltonicity material retained as a reusable but non-current module.
entries.title: Extremal Hamiltonicity and Johnson-density toolkit

entries.summary: Nine-vertex balanced-cover counting program: existence and multiplicity of 4|5 Hamiltonian partitions are sharpened from basic balanced coverage to large partition counts, then used to constrain trapped local 4|5 plateaux and synchronized replacements.
entries.title: Every nine-vertex boundary tournament has a balanced four-five two-cover

entries.summary: Reusable fractional path-cover machinery: LP duality and weighted capture, deletion-family averaging, dual slack accounting, laminar rounding, and sharp set-system obstructions to naive uncrossing.
entries.title: Fractional path-cover and LP toolkit

entries.summary: Deletion-cover compatibility toolkit: compatibility graphs, anchored incompatibility, support switches, relocation, low-degree density, uniform disagreement families, mixed-pattern normalization, and finite obstruction-color arguments for large families of deletion covers.
entries.title: Deletion-cover compatibility toolkit

entries.summary: Low-degree deletion-compatibility program: absent synchronized endpoint structure, compatibility degree is bounded; this yields large uniform-incompatibility families whose support patterns, coloring constraints, cubes, toggle moves, and mixed corridors are progressively normalized toward disagreement or transport.
entries.title: Either synchronized endpoint structure occurs or compatibility degree is at most four

entries.summary: Low-degree compatibility branch: four-colorability and clique closure of support-compatible cycles compress large deletion-label families to uniform incompatibility triples or a small set of four-cover support patterns, followed by mixed-triangle transport analysis.
entries.title: The low-degree compatibility branch is four-colorable

entries.summary: Exceptional four-cover compatibility patterns: when four incompatible deletion covers have no uniform triple, only P4/2K2-type support patterns survive; mixed triples and paired-switch corridors normalize those exceptions toward core disagreement or controlled support switching.
entries.title: Four incompatible deletion covers without a uniform triple have only two support patterns

entries.summary: Mixed compatibility-corridor branch: mixed incompatible triples normalize to one-switch or paired-switch support replacements; local insertion gadgets, endpoint replacements, and paired-transfer normalization then force five-set/reverse-cross structure, disturbance, or controlled support switching.
entries.title: Mixed incompatible triples have only a one-switch or paired-switch normal form

entries.summary: Three-label support-switch cube: odd split parity places six states in a one-defect cube; the missing antipodes, Hamiltonian core enlargements, adjacent-gap concentration, and pivot/toggle structure are then used to force order disagreement or bounded transport.
entries.title: The three-label support-switch configuration has an odd split parity

entries.summary: One-defect support-switch cube branch: a three-label support-switch triple occupies six cube states; deficit parity, support-switch Hamiltonian enlargements, adjacent-gap concentration, reverse-cross orientation, and extender-blocker toggles reduce the remaining cube geometry to bounded transport or order disagreement.
entries.title: A three-label support-switch triple occupies six vertices of the one-defect cube

entries.summary: Support-switch Hamiltonian-enlargement branch: the two parity types force core enlargements; adjacent-gap concentration, synchronized reverse crosses, opposite-orientation transpositions, and one-split extender-blocker toggles reduce the remaining geometry to bounded insertion windows, cross-swaps, or order disagreement.
entries.title: The two support-switch parity types force explicit Hamiltonian core enlargements

entries.summary: Reusable combinatorial-topology and matching toolkit: Sperner/Hex/Brouwer-type equivalences, Tucker and antipodal-coloring machinery, and hypergraph Hall/Ryser matching tools retained as general-purpose forcing methods for the project.
entries.title: Reusable combinatorial-topology and matching toolkit imported from LINP

entries.summary: Neutral endpoint-attachment swap branch: a one-block endpoint attachment yields reversal, a two-cover, or descent; the neutral case is a compatible omission swap whose cycles and triangles force order disagreement or strict quadratic descent.
entries.title: A one-block endpoint attachment restores to endpoint reversal, a two-cover, or quadratic descent

entries.summary: Five-side two-end locking branch: when a five-side admits no neutral swap, one long path becomes locked at both endpoints; trapped continuations then yield an equal-potential repartition or displayed-edge reversals on the long components.
entries.title: A five-side no-swap branch forces a two-sided endpoint lock on one long path

entries.summary: Path-cover surgery and comparison: exchange and replacement moves, minimum-imbalance and quadratic-minimum consequences, mandatory-support rigidity, inherited-class crossings, and finite reconfiguration steps.
entries.title: Path-cover surgery and comparison

entries.summary: General mandatory-triple normalization and cover-surgery consequences.
entries.title: A mandatory two-cover triple admits an endpoint-extension-minimal normalization

entries.summary: Two-cover inseparability toolkit: inseparable pairs admit cut obstructions, interior separations force crossings, and the equality-two-crossing case has a global support normal form.
entries.title: Two-cover inseparability classes

entries.summary: Foundational definitions and path conventions for the boundary-tournament program.
entries.title: Boundary tournaments and tight-path conventions

entries.summary: Reusable Astra-mined edge-order consequences, including the internal-rank classification for Hamiltonian edge-ordered K4s.
entries.title: Edge-ordered comparison model and one-half fence

entries.summary: Hamiltonian enlargement crossing toolkit: a one-vertex Hamiltonian enlargement forces every complementary deletion cover across the inherited cut; three-anchor windows sharpen this to multiple crossings, omitted-label reversals, or leave-and-return excursions, with endpoint Hamiltonicity providing the corresponding coarse transport alternative.
entries.title: A Hamiltonian one-vertex enlargement forces every complementary deletion cover to cross the underlying cut

entries.summary: Insertion and endpoint-replacement calculus: failed insertion, noninsertability, endpoint replacement, local spacing and obstruction menus, order disagreement, and short support migration.
entries.title: Insertion and endpoint-replacement calculus

entries.summary: Paired-noninsertability reduction beside a Hamiltonian four-set: two blocked exterior labels force a connector, opposite cross, order disagreement, or immediate descent, with unresolved cross residues carrying a rigid package of reversals and pivot hooks.
entries.title: Paired noninsertability beside a Hamiltonian four-set reduces locally to a connector, an opposite cross, disagreement, or descent at the generated state

entries.summary: Global noninsertability reversal branch: any vertex noninsertable into a displayed path reverses a displayed edge, and a family of such vertices yields a corresponding labelwise reversal family.
entries.title: Every globally noninsertable vertex reverses a displayed path edge

entries.summary: Near-Hamiltonian one-missing-vertex insertion branch: a path missing one vertex yields either a balanced cover or separated noninsertion obstructions, isolating the finite insertion geometry needed for subsequent endpoint-replacement arguments.
entries.title: A Hamilton path missing one vertex gives a balanced cover or two separated noninsertion obstructions

entries.summary: Local Hamilton-extension and match-set calculus: extension shells, common cores, endpoint-pair families, small Hamiltonian windows, local repartitions, and bounded lock/barrier alternatives.
entries.title: Local Hamilton-extension and match-set calculus

entries.summary: Four-of-six extension calculus from a fixed two-set across a four-set: multiple Hamiltonian three-of-four extensions feed common three-core, endpoint-pair, and interior-reversal consequences, especially for locally quadratic-minimal four-side configurations.
entries.title: A two-set has at least two Hamiltonian three-of-four extensions across any four-set

entries.summary: Fixed-pair orientation and extension-graph machinery: orientation classes form Hamiltonian four-extension cliques, giving dense prescribed-pair support families, exact perfect-matching orientation structure, witness bounds, and small-support consequences used throughout local extension arguments.
entries.title: Fixed-pair orientation classes are Hamiltonian four-extension cliques

entries.summary: Fixed-pair deletion stability: every fixed pair has many one- and two-label deletions with path-cover number two, and the descendant chain converts this abundance into structured extension and obstruction families around the fixed pair.
entries.title: Every fixed pair has a large family of one- and two-label path-cover-two deletions

entries.summary: Prescribed-pair alternating-five toolkit: every prescribed pair sits in an alternating Hamiltonian five-set with a stable complement family, yielding three-side realizations, deletion cubes, descending small-side moves, and reversal-carrying stable shells.
entries.title: Every prescribed pair lies in an alternating Hamiltonian five-set with a stable three-label complement family

entries.summary: Foundational minimum-counterexample consequences used throughout the two-cover program.
entries.title: Minimum-counterexample calculus

entries.summary: Prescribed-pair Hamiltonian four-window frontier in minimum counterexamples: every vertex pair lies in a Hamiltonian four-set with two-path complement, and the descendants exploit this universal pair coverage to generate reversal, crossing, and local obstruction structure.
entries.title: Every prescribed pair has a sharp linear star of Hamiltonian four-sets with two-path complements

entries.summary: Path restriction and intersection calculus: inherited-order behavior, endpoint extenders, common-gap gluing, deletion-order disagreement, support migration, reversal and tight-cycle localization, and the sharp-shell support-graph consequences that arise when order disturbance is sparse.
entries.title: Path restriction and intersection calculus

entries.summary: Longest-path deletion/order-disagreement program: Hamiltonian deletion abundance and non-Hamiltonian complement structure are used to force genuine order disagreement, universal small-set Hamiltonicity, or a sharp-shell support-graph regime where sparse deletion behavior can be analyzed combinatorially.
entries.title: Four Hamiltonian vertex deletions force order disagreement in every non-Hamiltonian set

entries.summary: Universal-six-set Hamiltonicity contradiction route: assuming no usable order disagreement forces every six-set Hamiltonian; the descendants then localize the resulting contradiction through deletion components, omitted-label crosses, tight cycles, genuine reversals, and sharp-shell support disturbance.
entries.title: Absence of order disagreement forces universal six-set Hamiltonicity

entries.summary: Order-disagreement extraction program: prove every minimum counterexample has nonvacuous disagreement, then localize it to overlapping short Hamilton paths, reversible consecutive pairs, reversing triples, or a classified minimal disagreement cycle suitable for downstream transport arguments.
entries.title: Every minimum counterexample contains order disagreement

entries.summary: Minimal order-disagreement classification: a minimal pair of conflicting tight-path orders is either localized or forms a pure two-arc tight cycle, with descendants resolving short crosses, omitted-label replacements, and the resulting local cycle geometry.
entries.title: A minimal order-disagreement pair is local or a pure two-arc tight cycle

entries.summary: Longest-path complement fork: a complement either has enough Hamiltonian deletions to force direct mixed crossing/order disagreement, or enters a deletion-sparse sharp-shell regime governed by support graphs, odd walks, neutral cuts, corridors, and repeated-label transport.
entries.title: A longest-path complement is either deletion-sparse or intrinsically order-disturbed

entries.summary: Sharp-shell support-graph program: encode good deletions by odd-graph degree and two-step support walks, analyze low-degree corridors, repeated labels, cut maps, and reciprocal rectangles, and force explicit transport disturbance when a clean sparse shell tries to persist.
entries.title: Sharp-shell good-deletion degree dictionary and low-degree expansion

entries.summary: Odd support-cycle disturbance branch in the sharp shell: odd cycles force a two-walk disturbance or repeated-label double crossing, and the descendants analyze six-edge corridors, clean cycles, repeated labels, decagon structure, and graph-level disturbance.
entries.title: Every odd support cycle forces two-walk disturbance or a repeated-label double crossing

entries.summary: Six-edge sharp-shell corridor branch: six odd support edges force local disturbance or repeated-label double crossing; the clean residue is classified through decagon/repeated-label shells, reciprocal rectangles, transport involutions, and bounded cycle completions.
entries.title: Six odd edges force local disturbance or a repeated-label double crossing

entries.summary: Clean degree-two shell branch: in the absence of immediate disturbance, repeated-label rectangles, fixed-core moving shells, decagon structure, rectangle transport, and cycle-completion constraints classify and eliminate the clean two-regular sharp-shell residue.
entries.title: A clean degree-two cycle without three-step label repetition forces odd degree at least three

entries.summary: Opposite-end neutral transport square: opposite endpoint deletion covers with intact inherited blocks force radius-two migration or disagreement; the neutral residue closes to a common-middle square whose synchronized complements either Hamiltonize or create doubled endpoint barriers.
entries.title: Opposite endpoint deletion covers with intact inherited blocks force a radius-two support migration or order disagreement

entries.summary: Quadratic component-size potential as a general reconfiguration toolkit. This region develops strict-descent criteria, neutral-transfer and restoration cycles, size-gap and complement-imbalance inequalities, global near-balance/staircase reductions, and dedicated two-, three-, four-, and five-side obstruction analyses. Nested branches isolate the sharp half-order extremal route and the local four-side and 4|5 plateau mechanisms.
entries.title: Quadratic component-size potential under path-cover moves

entries.summary: Global size-gap bypass in quadratic-minimum covers: a sufficiently imbalanced size profile forces a small non-Hamiltonian complement and several maximin consequences, providing a direct alternative to the balanced sharp-shell analysis.
entries.title: A global size gap forces a non-Hamiltonian complement of order at most twice the minimum side

entries.summary: Hamiltonian-enlargement complement-imbalance route: enlarging one component constrains every complementary two-cover; in the sharp half-order shell this yields the one-third minimum-side bound, its equality structure, secondary maximin normalization, and the canonical longest-path complement profile along the boundary case.
entries.title: Replacing one component by a Hamiltonian set h vertices larger forces a complement-imbalance penalty

entries.summary: Equitable quadratic-minimum branch: balanced three-cover profiles are absolute quadratic minima, and endpoint deletion probes then force multiple crossings, noninsertability, support migration, near-merges, or order disagreement.
entries.title: Equitable three-cover size profiles are absolute quadratic minima

entries.summary: Endpoint three-leaf route on a local 4|5 plateau: common five-set leaves rooted at both long endpoints lift to reachable four-sides and synchronized interior locks, then compress through common-core six-shell geometry or repeated long-interior obstruction.
entries.title: A locally minimal 4|5 plateau contains a three-leaf five-set star rooted at both long endpoints

entries.summary: Certified local machinery for a three-cover that minimizes the quadratic potential inside its pairwise-repartition component and has one four-vertex component beside long paths. Strict local descent is excluded, forcing two endpoint vertices of the four-vertex component to be noninsertable on each long middle path; paired obstruction windows then collapse to a Hamiltonian four- or five-set, a cyclic four-kernel, a tight cross triple, or a tight path connecting the same two exterior vertices.
entries.title: A four-side next to a long path either descends or creates two synchronized middle-path obstructions

entries.summary: Four-side endpoint-six obstruction branch: local minimality saturates the endpoint shell, the former fixed-endpoint perfect-matching residue is eliminated, and overlapping Hamiltonian windows force positioned pc2 squares whose endpoint branch descends or is bounded while the remaining branches expose standard support/order/internality disturbances.
entries.title: The hard four-side six-set yields five-window amplification or a fixed-endpoint matching shell

entries.summary: Local 4-by-5 quadratic plateau: equal-potential 4|5 repartitions generate a constrained plateau whose distinct states are crossed or singleton-adjacent; the resulting exchange graph forces support crossings, six-set order disagreement, or escape from the trapped local minimum.
entries.title: Every local 4|5|a quadratic minimum has a nontrivial equal-potential 4|5 repartition

entries.summary: Rigid local 4|5 plateau: a trapped 4|5|a quadratic minimum contains a nine-vertex residue whose two-covers all have profile 4|5, and the descendants force crossings, singleton-switch structure, endpoint blockade, or order disagreement.
entries.title: The nine-set of a trapped local 4|5|a minimum has only 4|5 two-covers

entries.summary: Foundational small-order Hamiltonicity and structure used throughout the two-cover program.
entries.title: Small-order Hamiltonicity and structure

entries.summary: Endpoint-pair Hamiltonicity graph branch: endpoint-pair Hamiltonicity has independence number at most two, yielding a dense complementary blocker family and a compact graph-theoretic encoding of local extension constraints.
entries.title: Endpoint-pair Hamiltonicity graphs have independence number at most two

entries.summary: Prescribed-terminal-pair balancing obstruction: balanced repartitions need not preserve a fixed terminal pair, and even common endpoint barriers need not force the hoped-for Hamiltonian five-window.
entries.title: Balanced repartitions need not preserve a prescribed terminal pair

entries.summary: Opposite-fixed-pair small-set classification: non-Hamiltonian four-sets with the forced opposite orientation have a rigid cyclic or edge-ordered form, and the descendant package uses two bad five-extensions to build overlapping four-sets, endpoint-overlap transport, and six-set deletion structure.
entries.title: An opposite-oriented fixed pair classifies every non-Hamiltonian four-set

entries.summary: Two-bad-five-extension branch of the small-set toolkit: failure of two five-extensions forces four opposite Hamiltonian deletions, which are organized into endpoint gap networks and finite endpoint-lock packages yielding transport, mixed support, tight cycles, or bounded residual configurations.
entries.title: Two non-Hamiltonian five-extensions force all four opposite five-deletions Hamiltonian

entries.summary: Four-side endpoint-gap reduction: a four-vertex side beside a path yields direct repartition descent, a bounded mixed Hamiltonian support, or a complete failed-insertion gap network whose reversals, connectors, and cycles provide the remaining closure mechanisms.
entries.title: A four-side beside a path reduces directly to transport, mixed support, or a complete gap network

entries.summary: Bad five-extension replacement branch: two failed one-vertex extensions of a Hamiltonian five-side force two-for-two Hamiltonian replacements and a six-set carrying several positioned good deletions.
entries.title: Two bad extensions of a Hamiltonian five-set force two-for-two Hamiltonian replacements

entries.summary: Certified neighboring-model theorem retained for analogy/generalization.
entries.title: Abstract ternary insertion theorem

entries.summary: Longest-path exterior-extension branch: a longest path has either a bi-endpoint Hamiltonian five-path or a small internal-reversal configuration; unless the reversal kernel appears, almost every exterior label extends to a five-path and large complements yield a six-set or common-four-core five-set family.
entries.title: A longest path has a bi-endpoint five-path or a four-vertex internal-reversal configuration

entries.summary: Reversal-support route: every minimum counterexample supplies a genuine reversing tight triple; dense Hamiltonian five-supports around that reversal are organized into stars and seven-vertex shells that force further reversal, order disagreement, or a bounded Hamiltonian output.
entries.title: Every minimum counterexample has a genuine reversing tight triple

entries.summary: Hamiltonian six-set two-label-square toolkit: a six-set with two-coverable complement contains a full square of two-label deletions; its endpoint coherence, internal-label alternatives, and four-core structure force crossing, descent, or order disagreement in the large-order regime.
entries.title: Every Hamiltonian six-set with two-coverable complement contains a full two-label square

entries.summary: Longest-path support and exchange toolkit: exterior vertices force displayed-edge reversals, while the sharp half-order shell admits an exact odd-graph exchange model used to encode and compare longest-support replacements.
entries.title: Longest-path support and exchange toolkit

entries.summary: Spanning-order and defect-line toolkit: reusable facts on defect centers and lines, swap stability, cyclic endpoint hooks, connector-or-transfer forks, minimum-side peels, matching-block endpoint kernels, and bounded propagation of defect structure.
entries.title: Spanning-order and defect-line toolkit

entries.summary: Span-three endpoint-hook and peel branch: a reversed cyclic endpoint hook yields synchronized cross-component hooks, connector-or-transfer forks, two-end peeling of a minimum side, and connector-free endpoint kernels whose blocked gap-two residue produces an order-incompatible transfer square.
entries.title: Every span-three ordering has a reversed cyclic endpoint hook

entries.summary: Exploratory proof routes and conjectures not yet integrated into the main two-cover proof, including longest-path outside-pair concentration, potential-based escape and exposure ideas, endpoint-incidence/Hall routes, deletion-fragmentation control, and common-pair or overlap separation mechanisms.
entries.title: Brainstorms
